actions.authority: district administration (superintendent Jose Dotres); board directive on guidelines 2025-08-12
actions.summary: Gave roughly 100,000 high-school students and their teachers Google Gemini for Education - the largest classroom AI deployment in the country when it was reported in May 2025 - after earlier blocking chatbots. The board then directed a tiered AI-use framework and discipline rules (August 2025).
actions.notes: effective_from approximates the spring-2025 rollout reported by the New York Times (2025-05-19); Google's case study is dated 2025-08-13. The 2025-08-12 board action asked a committee to report guidelines by 2025-10-01. Enrollment is district-wide; the action covers high schools. Enrollment figure is approximate.

actions.summary: Board voted 2026-07-29 to restrict most use of AI chatbots for all elementary students, cap PK-1 screen time to state-mandated testing and IEP/504 accommodations only, and direct the superintendent to put monitoring software on district devices district-wide with real-time alerts to the District Security Operations Center.
actions.notes: Corrected 2026-09-14: the earlier row dated this 2026-08-11 with a secondary source and no vote date. The board action was 2026-07-29; effective_from is the approximate first day of 2026-27. Chair Sarah Leonardi's motion originally covered PK-2 screen time; the adopted version stops at 1st grade. Enrollment approximate. AI chatbot restriction covers all elementary grades; the screen-time cap is PK-1 only.

actions.summary: First district AI policy: 'human in the loop' - teachers set written AI expectations each year, AI is off by default for submitted work unless the teacher permits it, only district-approved (closed) tools, and AI-detection software cannot be the sole basis for discipline. Built on 20,000 survey responses.
actions.notes: No parent opt-out, which one board member flagged. Adopted 2026-07-28, effective with the 2026-08-11 school year. Enrollment figure is approximate.

actions.summary: Board approved an Emerging Technologies policy and the district released its first AI Implementation Guide - critical thinking, data protection, academic integrity and access as the stated principles - developed by a cross-divisional AI governance team.
actions.notes: Announced 2025-06-13. The guide does not name tools or grade bands. Enrollment figure is approximate.
